blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) expects discussions on a possible minimum wage increase in Central Luzon to conclude before Christmas, as consultations among workers, employers, and government agencies are ongoing. Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino said negotiations for the region’s wage adjustment have taken longer because of its economic landscape, particularly its construction sector, major industries, and the presence of several organized labor groups. “Central Luzon is our hub. Clark is there. All the big industries are there,” Tolentino said on Wednesday, explaining why discussions on the proposed wage adjustment have required more time.
